# sinter

> sinter binds JSON APIs to plain HTML: keyed resources cached from the server, kept current from server events, rendered through <template> bindings, with optimistic mutations. A build step compiles annotated HTML into a page module; the browser runs no parser and no eval.

Package: @tiaforge-ui/sinter. Every directive is a `data-sn-*` attribute or an `<sn-*>` element. Anything else is a build error with a suggestion.

## Attributes

- `data-sn-state` (object literal): declares local reactive state for the element and its subtree
- `data-sn-let` (object literal {name: expression}): derived names for the element and its subtree, computed where they are read; later names may use earlier ones
- `data-sn-text` (value expression): sets textContent; never HTML
- `data-sn-attr` (object literal {href: …}): literal keys; null/false removes, true sets empty; URL values are checked; checked, selected, indeterminate and value also set the live property
- `data-sn-class` (object literal {unread: …}): toggles each class
- `data-sn-style` (object literal {'--color': …}): sets each property with style.setProperty
- `data-sn-show` (value expression): toggles the hidden attribute
- `data-sn-prop` (object literal): sets JS properties; custom elements only (one defined later gets them again through its setters)
- `data-sn-model` (state path): two-way binding for form controls
- `data-sn-for` (item in list | (item, i) in list): repeats a <template> per item
- `data-sn-key` (value expression): row identity; defaults to the resource key or object identity
- `data-sn-if` (value expression): renders a <template> while truthy
- `data-sn-else`: on a <template> directly after an if template
- `data-sn-listbox` (id of the suggestion list, or empty): on a text input: arrow keys mark a [role=option] of that list (empty: the nearest [role=listbox] around the input), Enter or Tab clicks it, Escape fires `dismiss`
- `data-sn-persist` (storage key): persists the model or state in localStorage under sn:
- `data-sn-get` (URL template): GET action; latest wins
- `data-sn-post` (URL template): POST action
- `data-sn-put` (URL template): PUT action
- `data-sn-patch` (URL template): PATCH action
- `data-sn-delete` (URL template): DELETE action
- `data-sn-call` (action call): local action: calls a function from the actions module, e.g. pgp.decrypt(msg); a handler starts it with run('id')
- `data-sn-body` (value expression): JSON request body; overrides form serialization
- `data-sn-trigger` (DOM event name): overrides the default trigger
- `data-sn-debounce` (milliseconds): delays the trigger, resets on each event; without a method, delays the element's data-sn-on-* handlers
- `data-sn-concurrency` (block | queue | latest): mutations only; default block for forms, queue otherwise
- `data-sn-optimistic` (handler expression): patch/upsert/remove calls applied before the request, kept on success, rolled back on failure
- `data-sn-then` (handler expression): runs after a 2xx response; $result = parsed body
- `data-sn-catch` (handler expression): runs after an error; $error = {status, body, message, detail}
- `data-sn-confirm` (value expression): asks this question before the action runs (configure({ confirm }), window.confirm by default); no question when falsy
- `data-sn-encoding` (json | form): form: the body (data-sn-body, arrays as repeated keys, or the form) goes as application/x-www-form-urlencoded
- `data-sn-apply` (off): turns write-through off for this mutation: its response is not applied to the resources it is about
- `data-sn-path` (URL patterns /a/:b …): on <html>: the path shapes this page is served for; `:name` segments appear read-only in $url
- `data-sn-data` (resource name): on <script type="application/json"> in <head>: initial data for a resource
- `data-sn-on-<event>` (handler expression): plain event handler, no request; e.g. data-sn-on-click
- `data-sn-on-keydown-<key>` (handler expression): runs only for that key (also on-keyup-<key>): modifiers first, the key last, e.g. data-sn-on-keydown-j, -shift-n (N), -mod-enter (Ctrl, Cmd on Apple), -escape, -question (?); matches KeyboardEvent.key; other Ctrl/Alt/Meta held do not match; an ancestor's filter skips keys typed into fields; a match calls preventDefault()
- `data-sn-debounce-<event>` (milliseconds): delays only that event's data-sn-on-<event> handler (it runs with the last event); e.g. data-sn-debounce-input

Key filters (`data-sn-on-keydown-<modifiers->key`, `data-sn-on-keyup-…`): modifiers `ctrl`, `alt`, `shift`, `meta`, `mod`, then one key: `a`–`z`, `0`–`9`, `escape`, `enter`, `tab`, `space`, `backspace`, `delete`, `insert`, `home`, `end`, `pageup`, `pagedown`, `arrowup`, `arrowdown`, `arrowleft`, `arrowright`, `contextmenu`, `f1`–`f12`, and characters by name: `slash` (`/`), `backslash` (`\`), `question` (`?`), `period` (`.`), `comma` (`,`), `semicolon` (`;`), `colon` (`:`), `quote` (`'`), `backquote` (``` ` ```), `minus` (`-`), `plus` (`+`), `equal` (`=`), `asterisk` (`*`), `bracketleft` (`[`), `bracketright` (`]`). Attribute names are lowercase, so N is `shift-n`; Shift is not checked for characters (`question` is ? however it is typed). Filters on an ancestor skip keys typed into fields (input, textarea, select, contenteditable) and Enter/Space on buttons and links; a filter on the field itself runs. A match calls `preventDefault()`; on one element, filters and a plain `data-sn-on-keydown` run in attribute order. The nearest element that handles an event wins: for clicks and other native events any handler or action that ran, for keys a matching filter, an action, a debounced handler, or a plain handler that called `$event.preventDefault()`; a key a plain handler does not prevent goes on to its ancestors, so a grid's arrow-key handler that prevents only the arrows leaves N to `<body data-sn-on-keydown-shift-n>`. Page-wide shortcuts go on `<body>`. Bubbling custom events (`emit()`, islands' `CustomEvent`s, `sn-error`, `dismiss`) are notifications: every element from the target up with a handler for one runs, inner first, until a handler calls `$event.preventDefault()` (the rest of that element's handlers and its action still run); `emit()` and `dismiss` are cancelable, and an island makes its events stoppable with `cancelable: true`. Debounced handlers and actions pass them on. A custom event that does not bubble, and a plain `Event`, go to the nearest element only. There is no `stop()`; `stopPropagation()` does not end the walk.

## Elements

- `<sn-resource>` `name`, `src`, `call`, `each`, `key`, `items`, `total`, `order`, `when`, `paginate`, `page-size`, `size-param`, `cursor`, `direction-param`, `direction-values`, `page-param`, `offset-param`, `type`, `cache`, `then`: a named, page-wide cache of server data; `cache` (or `cache="10m"`) shows the data from the last page load at once, then revalidates. `then` is a handler run after each successful load (`$result`: what it loaded; the state around the resource in scope). Loading needs no attributes: concurrent loads of one URL share a request, a `src` change aborts the running one (latest wins), a change typed into a text field waits 250 ms for the next keystroke, a resource only dialogs read is requested with low priority, and a bfcache restore or going back online refetches
- `<sn-sync>` `src`: one server event stream
- `<sn-event>` `name`, `resource`, `op`, `item`, `set`, `when`, `fallback`, `then`, `type`: maps one server event to a change message; child of <sn-sync>. `then` is a handler run after the change (payload fields and the state around the sync in scope), e.g. close('detail'); with `then`, `resource` and `op` may be left out
- `<sn-include>` `src`: inlines a partial at build time

## Expressions and scope

- Attribute values are JavaScript expressions, checked at build time. Value expressions (text, attr, class, show, for, if, key, body, state, URL interpolations) cannot assign, use `++`, `delete`, `await` or `import()`.
- Handlers (`data-sn-on-*`, `then`, `catch`) are statements separated by `;`: assignments to state, `$url.<param>` and `$locale`, and calls. No declarations or loops.
- A handler cannot call an action function (SN203). To start an action from a handler (a key filter, `data-sn-then`, `<sn-resource then>`), give the action element an `id` and call `run('id')`; the element's busy state, concurrency, optimistic layer and `then`/`catch` apply. A hidden carrier works: `<span hidden id="mark-read" data-sn-call="mail.markRead(open)"></span>`. See the recipe "Run an action from a handler".
- `then` on `<sn-event>` is a handler run after the event's change is applied: payload fields are bare names, the state around the `<sn-sync>` is in scope and assignable, and so are its `data-sn-let` names (read-only; state and lets win over payload fields of the same name), store functions work (`close('id')` names its dialog: there is no element). With `then`, `resource` and `op` may be left out.
- `then` on `<sn-resource>` is a handler run after each successful load (first load, `refresh()`, refetch events, `src` changes, every `page()`; per source for `each`), not for cached data shown at once, failed loads or optimistic/event changes. `$result` is what the load stored (what `items` selects; the page just loaded). The state around the resource is in scope and assignable; `close('id')` names its dialog. It runs on every refetch, so a once-only handler guards itself, one step per guard: `then="draft = $result ?? draft; $result && showModal('compose')"`.
- `data-sn-optimistic` may only call `patch`, `upsert`, `remove`. The change shows at once, stays when the request succeeds (committed under what `then` writes) and is rolled back when it fails.
- A name resolves innermost first: loop variables, then the nearest `data-sn-state`, then resources, then magic names, helpers and store functions, then JavaScript globals. Browser APIs (`window`, `document`, `fetch`, timers, …) are refused: use an island.
- Resources are read-only: copy an item with `structuredClone(c)` to edit it, write with `patch()`.
- Helpers are plain function calls, never pipes: `date()`, `time()`, `datetime()`, `relative()`, `number()`, `bytes()`. Helper namespaces: `m.inbox_title()`.
- URL templates: `/api/x?id={c.id}`; interpolations are URL-encoded; the template must start with a literal `/path` or `https://origin`. A whole query value that is `null`/`undefined` or an empty array leaves the parameter out; an array is a repeated key (`?cal={cals}` → `cal=a&cal=b`); an array in the path is refused.
- Use `$now` instead of `Date.now()` so bindings update.

## What belongs in markup

- Markup holds filters, conditions, single assignments and short calls. Logic goes into a helper when it computes a value (pure: unit-test it without a page), or into an action when it has side effects (`data-sn-call`).
- Handlers apply a helper's result to state: `data-sn-on-click="sel = rowClick($event, sel, f.id, ids)"`, not branches on `$event.shiftKey` in the attribute. See the row selection recipe.
- One step per condition: `open && close('detail')` is fine; `a && (b = null, close())` is not: split it into statements, let the dialog's `data-sn-on-close` reset state, or compute the new state in a helper.
- Warning SN507 (`complex-expression`) flags expressions that outgrew markup and names the limit: statements per handler (4), comma sequences (0), steps behind one `&&`/`||`/`?:` statement (1), `?:` nesting (2), operations in an arrow function (8), operations per expression (15). `sinter({ complexity: { …, level: 'warn' | 'error' | 'off' } })` changes them.

## Magic names

`$event`, `$el`, `$url`, `$now`, `$locale`, `$result`, `$error`, `$meta`. `$event` in handlers, `$result` in `then`, `$error` (`{status, body, message}`) in `catch`; `$meta.<resource>` has `loading`, `error`, `loadedAt`, `pending`, `total`, and with `paginate`: `page` (offset), `pages`, `from`, `to`, `hasPrev`, `hasNext`.

## Store functions

`refresh()`, `upsert()`, `patch()`, `remove()`, `page()`, `showModal()`, `close()`, `reset()`, `emit()`, `run()`: `refresh('name')` (or several: `refresh('a', 'b')`), `upsert('name', item)`, `patch('name', item, {…})`, `remove('name', item)`, `page('name', 'next' | 'prev' | 'first' | 'last' | n)` (a page number needs offset mode or keyset with `offset-param`, else SN304; a computed direction such as `$event.shiftKey ? 'prev' : 'next'` works everywhere, typed by `sinter check`; `prev` does nothing while `hasPrev` is false and `next` while `hasNext` is false, in every mode, so paging needs no `$meta` guard; `first` and `last` always load), `showModal('id')` opens a dialog by its literal id, `close()` the nearest dialog or `close('id')` that one, `reset()` the nearest form, `emit('event', detail)` (a bubbling, cancelable `CustomEvent`), `run('id')` starts the action of the element with that literal id (SN311), as its trigger would but with `$event` null; a form is submitted (`requestSubmit()`, validation runs); a disabled or inert element does nothing; it returns nothing, results go to the element's `then`/`catch`. The resource name may be chosen from literals: `page(searching ? 'results' : 'messages', 'next')`, `||`/`??` between literals, or a `data-sn-let` name whose value is one (`data-sn-let="{ shown: searching ? 'results' : 'messages' }"`, then `page(shown, 'next')`, `$meta[shown].hasNext`); every name it can take is checked like a literal; a state variable or helper result is SN301 (make it a `?:`).

## Write-through

A mutation's 2xx response is applied to the store by itself, before `then` runs (the `apply` module, loaded when a page has something to apply). With an OpenAPI spec: an object of a named schema in the response (`{article: Article}`) patches the same-key item in every list of that schema and what the URL named (`{article.slug}` names the single `article`; `{article.author.username}` also names `article.author`, a Profile); a POST to exactly a list's current URL inserts the created item (the response's, else body + returned key, else a refetch; a filtered or paginated list is never inserted into); a PUT/PATCH body patches the entity the URL named. Without a spec: a DELETE of a row's URL (the list's URL plus one segment, from `c.id` with `c in comments`) removes the row, and a PUT/PATCH body patches the row when its keys are fields of the row. Patches merge and skip unchanged fields; `then` writes land on top. So `data-sn-then="patch('articles', a, $result.article)"`, `upsert('comments', $result.comment)` and `remove('comments', c)` are not written (SN510 says so); `data-sn-optimistic` is still how a change shows before the answer. `data-sn-apply="off"` turns it off for one element.

## Diagnostics

`SN101 unknown-attribute`, `SN102 wrong-element`, `SN103 missing-key`, `SN104 unsupported-model`, `SN201 unknown-identifier`, `SN202 forbidden-global`, `SN203 side-effect`, `SN204 optimistic-scope`, `SN205 resource-mutation`, `SN206 unknown-namespace-member`, `SN207 unsafe-sink`, `SN208 type-error`, `SN209 name-conflict`, `SN301 unknown-resource`, `SN302 duplicate-resource`, `SN303 unknown-meta-field`, `SN304 keyset-jump`, `SN305 include-not-found`, `SN306 include-cycle`, `SN307 openapi-invalid`, `SN308 unknown-schema-field`, `SN309 unknown-dialog`, `SN310 unknown-action`, `SN311 unknown-run-target`, `SN401 parse-error`, `SN501 unused-resource`, `SN502 non-reactive-value`, `SN503 data-bound-id`, `SN504 untyped-resource`, `SN505 unknown-query-param`, `SN506 untyped-event`, `SN507 complex-expression`, `SN509 run-cycle`, `SN510 redundant-write`.

## Recipes

Each recipe comes with its test; copy both.

### List with filter

```html
<sn-resource name="people" src="/api/people" items="people" key="id" order="name"></sn-resource>

<section data-sn-state="{ q: '' }">
  <input type="search" placeholder="Search" data-sn-model="q">
  <p data-sn-show="$meta.people.loading" aria-busy="true">Loading…</p>
  <ul>
    <template data-sn-for="p in people.filter(p => p.name.toLowerCase().includes(q.toLowerCase()))">
      <li data-sn-text="p.name"></li>
    </template>
  </ul>
</section>
```

```ts
import { expect, test } from 'vitest';
import { render, mockRequests } from '@tiaforge-ui/sinter/testing';
import page from './list-filter.html?raw';


test('filters the list as you type', async () => {
  const requests = mockRequests({ 'GET /api/people': { people: [{ id: 1, name: 'Bob' }, { id: 2, name: 'Ada' }] } });
  const { root, flush, settle } = await render(page, { requests });
  await settle();
  expect([...root.querySelectorAll('li')].map((li) => li.textContent)).toEqual(['Ada', 'Bob']);

  const input = root.querySelector('input')!;
  input.value = 'ad';
  input.dispatchEvent(new Event('input', { bubbles: true }));
  await flush();
  expect([...root.querySelectorAll('li')].map((li) => li.textContent)).toEqual(['Ada']);
});
```

### Form dialog with repeatable fields

```html
<sn-resource name="people" src="/api/people" key="id" order="name"></sn-resource>

<section data-sn-state="{ draft: null }">
  <button data-sn-on-click="draft = {name: '', emails: [{value: ''}]}" commandfor="edit" command="show-modal">New</button>
  <ul>
    <template data-sn-for="p in people">
      <li>
        <span data-sn-text="p.name"></span>
        <button data-sn-on-click="draft = structuredClone(p)" commandfor="edit" command="show-modal">Edit</button>
      </li>
    </template>
  </ul>

  <dialog id="edit">
    <form data-sn-post="/api/people" data-sn-body="draft"
          data-sn-then="upsert('people', $result); draft = null; close()"
          data-sn-catch="emit('toast', $error.message)">
      <input data-sn-model="draft.name" required>
      <template data-sn-for="(e, i) in draft.emails">
        <input type="email" data-sn-model="draft.emails[i].value">
      </template>
      <button type="button" data-sn-on-click="draft.emails.push({value: ''})">Add email</button>
      <button type="submit">Save</button>
    </form>
  </dialog>
</section>
```

```ts
import { expect, test } from 'vitest';
import { render, mockRequests } from '@tiaforge-ui/sinter/testing';
import page from './form-dialog.html?raw';


test('saves the draft and upserts the result', async () => {
  const requests = mockRequests({
    'GET /api/people': [],
    'POST /api/people': (call) => ({ id: 1, ...(call.body as object) }),
  });
  const { root, flush, settle } = await render(page, { requests });
  await settle();
  root.querySelector('button')!.click();               // New
  const dialog = root.querySelector('dialog')!;
  dialog.showModal();
  dialog.dispatchEvent(new Event('toggle'));
  await flush();

  const [name, email] = root.querySelectorAll('dialog input');
  (name as HTMLInputElement).value = 'Ada';
  name!.dispatchEvent(new Event('input', { bubbles: true }));
  (email as HTMLInputElement).value = 'ada@example.com';
  email!.dispatchEvent(new Event('input', { bubbles: true }));
  root.querySelector('form')!.requestSubmit();
  await settle();

  expect(requests.calls.at(-1)!.body).toEqual({ name: 'Ada', emails: [{ value: 'ada@example.com' }] });
  expect(root.querySelector('li span')!.textContent).toBe('Ada');
  expect(dialog.open).toBe(false);
});
```

### SSE sync

```html
<sn-resource name="people" src="/api/people" key="id" order="name"></sn-resource>

<main data-sn-state="{ sel: null }">
  <sn-sync src="/api/events">
    <sn-event name="person_updated" resource="people" op="upsert" item="person" fallback="refetch"></sn-event>
    <!-- after the removal: close the dialog if it shows that person (closing clears `sel`) -->
    <sn-event name="person_removed" resource="people" op="remove"
              then="sel?.id === id && close('person')"></sn-event>
  </sn-sync>

  <ul>
    <template data-sn-for="p in people">
      <li><button data-sn-on-click="sel = p; showModal('person')" data-sn-text="p.name"></button></li>
    </template>
  </ul>
  <dialog id="person" data-sn-on-close="sel = null"><h2 data-sn-text="sel?.name"></h2></dialog>
</main>
```

```ts
import { expect, test } from 'vitest';
import { render, mockRequests, mockStream } from '@tiaforge-ui/sinter/testing';
import page from './sse-sync.html?raw';


test('applies server events to the list', async () => {
  const requests = mockRequests({ 'GET /api/people': [{ id: 1, name: 'Bob' }] });
  const stream = mockStream();
  const { root, flush, settle } = await render(page, { requests, streams: { '/api/events': stream } });
  await settle();

  stream.emit('person_updated', { person: { id: 2, name: 'Ada' } });
  stream.emit('person_removed', { id: 1 });
  await flush();
  expect([...root.querySelectorAll('li')].map((li) => li.textContent)).toEqual(['Ada']);
});

test('a removed person closes the dialog that shows them', async () => {
  const requests = mockRequests({ 'GET /api/people': [{ id: 1, name: 'Bob' }, { id: 2, name: 'Ada' }] });
  const stream = mockStream();
  const { root, flush, settle } = await render(page, { requests, streams: { '/api/events': stream } });
  await settle();
  root.querySelector('button')!.click();   // Ada
  await flush();
  const dialog = root.querySelector('dialog')!;
  expect(dialog.open).toBe(true);

  stream.emit('person_removed', { id: 1 });
  await flush();
  expect(dialog.open).toBe(true);
  stream.emit('person_removed', { id: 2 });
  await flush();
  expect(dialog.open).toBe(false);
});
```

### Optimistic toggle

```html
<sn-resource name="messages" src="/api/messages" key="id"></sn-resource>

<template data-sn-for="m in messages">
  <article>
    <span data-sn-text="m.subject"></span>
    <button data-sn-patch="/api/messages/{m.id}"
            data-sn-body="{is_flagged: !m.is_flagged}"
            data-sn-optimistic="patch('messages', m, {is_flagged: !m.is_flagged})"
            data-sn-attr="{'aria-pressed': m.is_flagged ? 'true' : 'false'}">★</button>
  </article>
</template>
```

```ts
import { expect, test } from 'vitest';
import { render, mockRequests } from '@tiaforge-ui/sinter/testing';
import page from './optimistic-toggle.html?raw';


test('flags at once and rolls back when the server refuses', async () => {
  const requests = mockRequests({
    'GET /api/messages': [{ id: 1, subject: 'Hi', is_flagged: false }],
    'PATCH /api/messages/1': { status: 500 },
  });
  const { root, flush, settle } = await render(page, { requests });
  await settle();
  const star = root.querySelector('button')!;

  star.click();
  await flush();
  expect(star.getAttribute('aria-pressed')).toBe('true');   // optimistic

  await settle();
  expect(star.getAttribute('aria-pressed')).toBe('false');  // rolled back
});

test('keeps the flag when the server accepts it', async () => {
  const requests = mockRequests({
    'GET /api/messages': [{ id: 1, subject: 'Hi', is_flagged: false }],
    'PATCH /api/messages/1': null,
  });
  const { root, settle } = await render(page, { requests });
  await settle();
  const star = root.querySelector('button')!;

  star.click();
  await settle();
  expect(star.getAttribute('aria-pressed')).toBe('true');   // committed: no flip back
});
```

### Pagination

```html
<sn-resource name="messages" src="/api/messages" items="messages" total="total" key="id"
  paginate="keyset" page-size="2" cursor="{before: id}"></sn-resource>

<ul>
  <template data-sn-for="m in messages"><li data-sn-text="m.subject"></li></template>
</ul>
<nav>
  <button data-sn-on-click="page('messages', 'prev')" data-sn-attr="{disabled: !$meta.messages.hasPrev}">‹</button>
  <span data-sn-text="`${$meta.messages.from}–${$meta.messages.to} of ${$meta.messages.total}`"></span>
  <button data-sn-on-click="page('messages', 'next')" data-sn-attr="{disabled: !$meta.messages.hasNext}">›</button>
</nav>
```

```ts
import { expect, test } from 'vitest';
import { render, mockRequests } from '@tiaforge-ui/sinter/testing';
import page from './pagination.html?raw';

const all = [5, 4, 3, 2, 1].map((id) => ({ id, subject: `m${id}` }));

test('moves to the next page with a cursor', async () => {
  const requests = mockRequests({
    'GET /api/messages': (call) => {
      const q = new URL(call.url, 'http://x').searchParams;
      const before = Number(q.get('before') ?? Infinity);
      const items = q.get('direction') === 'next' ? all.filter((m) => m.id < before) : all;
      return { messages: items.slice(0, Number(q.get('limit'))), total: all.length };
    },
  });
  const { root, settle } = await render(page, { requests });
  await settle();
  expect(root.querySelector('span')!.textContent).toBe('1–2 of 5');

  root.querySelector<HTMLButtonElement>('nav button:last-of-type')!.click();
  await settle();
  expect([...root.querySelectorAll('li')].map((li) => li.textContent)).toEqual(['m3', 'm2']);
  expect(root.querySelector('span')!.textContent).toBe('3–4 of 5');
  expect(requests.calls.at(-1)!.url).toBe('/api/messages?before=4&limit=2&direction=next');
});
```

### SignalR (or another transport) for <sn-sync>

```html
<!-- The page is the same as with SSE: only the configured transport differs (signalr-transport.js). -->
<sn-resource name="people" src="/api/people" key="id" order="name"></sn-resource>

<sn-sync src="/hubs/people">
  <sn-event name="person_updated" resource="people" op="upsert" item="person"></sn-event>
  <sn-event name="person_removed" resource="people" op="remove"></sn-event>
</sn-sync>

<ul>
  <template data-sn-for="p in people"><li data-sn-text="p.name"></li></template>
</ul>
```

```js
// SignalR transport for <sn-sync>, in your app (sinter does not depend on @microsoft/signalr).
// In src/sinter.config.js:
//
//   import { HubConnectionBuilder } from '@microsoft/signalr';
//   import { configure } from '@tiaforge-ui/sinter';
//   import { signalRTransport } from './signalr-transport.js';
//
//   configure({
//     transport: (url) => url.startsWith('/hubs/')
//       ? signalRTransport(() => new HubConnectionBuilder().withUrl(url).build())
//       : undefined,
//   });
//
// Server: `await Clients.All.SendAsync("person_updated", new { person })`; the first argument is
// the payload. Hub method names are case-insensitive in SignalR, so keep event names distinct in
// more than case. Do not call withAutomaticReconnect(): sinter reconnects (session probe, backoff,
// refetch of everything the stream feeds), and two reconnect loops would race. Auth is the hub's:
// cookies, or withUrl(url, { accessTokenFactory }); request middleware does not apply.

/** @param {() => import('@microsoft/signalr').HubConnection} build a new, unstarted connection */
export function signalRTransport(build) {
  let hub = null;
  let deliver = null;
  const names = new Set();
  const add = (name) => {
    if (!hub || names.has(name)) return;
    names.add(name);
    const h = hub;
    h.on(name, (payload) => { if (hub === h) deliver(name, payload ?? null); });
  };
  return {
    connect(url, onEvent, onState, initial) {
      const h = hub = build();
      deliver = onEvent;
      names.clear();
      for (const n of initial) add(n);
      h.onclose(() => { if (hub === h) { hub = null; onState('error'); } });
      h.start().then(() => { if (hub === h) onState('open'); }, () => { if (hub === h) { hub = null; onState('error'); } });
    },
    listen: add,
    close() {
      const h = hub;
      hub = null; // nothing is reported after close()
      h?.stop().catch(() => {});
    },
  };
}
```

```ts
import { afterEach, expect, test } from 'vitest';
import { configure } from '@tiaforge-ui/sinter';
import { render, mockRequests } from '@tiaforge-ui/sinter/testing';
import { signalRTransport } from './signalr-transport.js';
import page from './signalr.html?raw';

// A stand-in for HubConnection: the test calls invoke() where the server would call SendAsync().
function fakeHub() {
  const handlers = new Map<string, (payload: unknown) => void>();
  let onclose = () => {};
  return {
    started: false,
    on(name: string, fn: (payload: unknown) => void) { handlers.set(name, fn); },
    onclose(fn: () => void) { onclose = fn; },
    async start() { this.started = true; },
    async stop() { this.started = false; },
    invoke(name: string, payload: unknown) { handlers.get(name)?.(payload); },
    lose() { this.started = false; onclose(); },
  };
}

afterEach(() => configure({ transport: null }));

test('applies hub messages to the list', async () => {
  const hubs: Array<ReturnType<typeof fakeHub>> = [];
  configure({ transport: (url) => (url.startsWith('/hubs/') ? signalRTransport(() => { hubs.push(fakeHub()); return hubs.at(-1) as never; }) : undefined) });
  const requests = mockRequests({ 'GET /api/people': [{ id: 1, name: 'Bob' }] });
  const { root, flush, settle, advance } = await render(page, { requests });
  await settle();
  expect(hubs[0]!.started).toBe(true);

  hubs[0]!.invoke('person_updated', { person: { id: 2, name: 'Ada' } });
  hubs[0]!.invoke('person_removed', { id: 1 });
  await flush();
  expect([...root.querySelectorAll('li')].map((li) => li.textContent)).toEqual(['Ada']);

  // a lost connection: sinter reconnects with a new hub and refetches what the stream feeds
  hubs[0]!.lose();
  await advance(2000); // the backoff (1 s ± jitter) before reconnecting
  await settle();
  expect(hubs).toHaveLength(2);
  expect(requests.calls.filter((c) => c.path === '/api/people')).toHaveLength(2);
});
```

### Cached list across page loads

```html
<!-- `cache`: the next page load shows this list at once, then revalidates.
     `$meta.inbox.loading` with data present means "updating"; `$meta.inbox.loadedAt`
     stays null until the server has answered on this page. -->
<sn-resource name="inbox" src="/api/messages?folder=inbox" key="id" order="-date" cache="1h"></sn-resource>

<p data-sn-show="$meta.inbox.loading && inbox.length">Updating…</p>
<ul>
  <template data-sn-for="m in inbox">
    <li data-sn-text="m.subject"></li>
  </template>
</ul>
```

```ts
import { expect, test } from 'vitest';
import { render, mockRequests, memoryStorage } from '@tiaforge-ui/sinter/testing';
import page from './cached-list.html?raw';

const subjects = (root: HTMLElement) => [...root.querySelectorAll('li')].map((li) => li.textContent);

test('the next page load shows the cached list while it revalidates', async () => {
  // one tab: the same sessionStorage for both page loads
  const session = memoryStorage();
  const first = await render(page, { session, requests: mockRequests({
    'GET /api/messages': [{ id: 1, subject: 'Welcome', date: '2026-01-01' }],
  }) });
  await first.settle();

  const { root, settle } = await render(page, { session, requests: mockRequests({
    'GET /api/messages': [{ id: 2, subject: 'Lunch?', date: '2026-01-02' }, { id: 1, subject: 'Welcome', date: '2026-01-01' }],
  }) });
  expect(subjects(root)).toEqual(['Welcome']);                    // cached, before any response
  expect(root.querySelector('p')!.hidden).toBe(false);            // "Updating…"

  await settle();
  expect(subjects(root)).toEqual(['Lunch?', 'Welcome']);
  expect(root.querySelector('p')!.hidden).toBe(true);
});
```

### Local actions: hash a file, then upload it

```html
<section data-sn-state="{ file: null, url: '', error: '' }">
  <sn-resource name="digest" call="sha256(file)" when="file"></sn-resource>

  <input type="file" data-sn-on-change="file = $el.files[0] ?? null; url = ''">
  <p data-sn-show="$meta.digest.loading">Hashing…</p>
  <code data-sn-text="digest"></code>

  <button data-sn-call="upload(file, digest)" data-sn-attr="{disabled: !digest}"
          data-sn-then="url = $result.url; error = ''" data-sn-catch="error = $error.message">Upload</button>
  <a data-sn-show="url" data-sn-attr="{href: url}">Uploaded</a>
  <p role="alert" data-sn-text="error"></p>
</section>
```

```js
// src/sinter.actions.js: functions pages call with data-sn-call and <sn-resource call>.
// The last argument is sinter's context; with JSDoc types, `sinter check` checks the calls.
/** @import { CallContext } from '@tiaforge-ui/sinter' */

/**
 * The file's SHA-256 as hex; choosing another file aborts the running hash through ctx.signal.
 * @param {File} file
 * @param {CallContext} ctx
 * @returns {Promise<string>}
 */
export async function sha256(file, ctx) {
  const bytes = await file.arrayBuffer();
  ctx.signal.throwIfAborted();
  const hash = await crypto.subtle.digest('SHA-256', bytes);
  return [...new Uint8Array(hash)].map((b) => b.toString(16).padStart(2, '0')).join('');
}

/**
 * ctx.request goes through the app's middleware (headers, 401 handling, allowed origins).
 * @param {File} file
 * @param {string} digest
 * @param {CallContext} ctx
 * @returns {Promise<{ url: string }>}
 */
export async function upload(file, digest, ctx) {
  const form = new FormData();
  form.append('file', file);
  form.append('sha256', digest);
  return /** @type {Promise<{ url: string }>} */ (ctx.request('/api/uploads', { method: 'POST', body: form }));
}
```

```ts
import { expect, test } from 'vitest';
import { checkPage } from '@tiaforge-ui/sinter/check';
import { render, mockRequests } from '@tiaforge-ui/sinter/testing';
import * as actions from './local-actions.actions.js';
import source from './local-actions.actions.js?raw';
import page from './local-actions.html?raw';

const DIGEST = 'ba7816bf8f01cfea414140de5dae2223b00361a396177a9cb410ff61f20015ad'; // sha256('abc')

function choose(input: HTMLInputElement, file: File) {
  Object.defineProperty(input, 'files', { value: [file], configurable: true });
  input.dispatchEvent(new Event('change', { bubbles: true }));
}

test('hashes the chosen file, then uploads it with its digest', async () => {
  const requests = mockRequests({ 'POST /api/uploads': { url: '/files/1' } });
  const { root, settle } = await render(page, { actions, requests });
  const button = root.querySelector('button')!;
  expect(button.disabled).toBe(true);

  choose(root.querySelector('input')!, new File(['abc'], 'abc.txt'));
  await settle();
  expect(root.querySelector('code')!.textContent).toBe(DIGEST);
  expect(button.disabled).toBe(false);

  button.click();
  await settle();
  expect((requests.calls[0]!.body as FormData).get('sha256')).toBe(DIGEST);
  expect(root.querySelector('a')!.getAttribute('href')).toBe('/files/1');
});

test('a failed upload shows the server message', async () => {
  const requests = mockRequests({ 'POST /api/uploads': { status: 413, body: { message: 'File too large' } } });
  const { root, settle } = await render(page, { actions, requests });
  choose(root.querySelector('input')!, new File(['abc'], 'abc.txt'));
  await settle();
  root.querySelector('button')!.click();
  await settle();
  expect(root.querySelector('[role=alert]')!.textContent).toBe('File too large');
});

test('sinter check: arguments are checked against the actions', () => {
  const files = { 'src/sinter.actions.js': source };
  expect(checkPage(page, { files })).toEqual([]);
  const [d] = checkPage(page.replace('upload(file, digest)', 'upload(file)'), { files });
  expect([d!.code, d!.message]).toEqual(['SN208', expect.stringContaining("is not assignable to type '[file: File, digest: string]'")]);
});
```

### Keyboard shortcuts

```html
<!doctype html>
<html>
<body data-sn-state="{ cursor: 0, open: null, marked: [] }"
      data-sn-on-keydown-j="cursor = Math.min(cursor + 1, messages.length - 1)"
      data-sn-on-keydown-k="cursor = Math.max(cursor - 1, 0)"
      data-sn-on-keydown-enter="open = messages[cursor]"
      data-sn-on-keydown-escape="open = null"
      data-sn-on-keydown-ctrl-space="marked = marked.includes(cursor) ? marked.filter(i => i !== cursor) : [...marked, cursor]"
      data-sn-on-keydown-slash="$el.querySelector('input').focus()">
  <sn-resource name="messages" src="/api/messages" items="messages" key="id"></sn-resource>
  <!-- in the field, j, k and / are typed; its own Escape filter leaves it -->
  <input type="search" placeholder="Search (/)" data-sn-on-keydown-escape="$el.blur()">
  <ul>
    <template data-sn-for="(m, i) in messages">
      <li data-sn-class="{cursor: i === cursor, marked: marked.includes(i)}" data-sn-text="m.subject"></li>
    </template>
  </ul>
  <article data-sn-show="open" data-sn-text="open && open.subject"></article>
</body>
</html>
```

```ts
import { expect, test } from 'vitest';
import { render, mockRequests } from '@tiaforge-ui/sinter/testing';
import page from './keyboard-shortcuts.html?raw';

const key = (el: Element, k: string, init: KeyboardEventInit = {}) =>
  el.dispatchEvent(new KeyboardEvent('keydown', { key: k, bubbles: true, cancelable: true, ...init }));

test('j/k move the cursor, Ctrl+Space marks, Enter opens, Escape closes; keys typed in the search field stay there', async () => {
  const requests = mockRequests({ 'GET /api/messages': { messages: [{ id: 1, subject: 'Hello' }, { id: 2, subject: 'Lunch?' }] } });
  const { root, flush, settle } = await render(page, { requests });
  await settle();
  const body = root /* the <body> */, rows = () => [...root.querySelectorAll('li')];
  key(body, 'j');
  key(body, ' ', { ctrlKey: true });
  key(body, 'Enter');
  await flush();
  expect(rows().map((li) => li.className)).toEqual(['', 'cursor marked']);
  expect(root.querySelector('article')!.textContent).toBe('Lunch?');

  key(root.querySelector('input')!, 'k');  // typing a k
  key(body, 'Escape');
  await flush();
  expect(rows()[1]!.className).toBe('cursor marked');
  expect(root.querySelector('article')!.hidden).toBe(true);

  key(body, '/');
  expect(root.ownerDocument.activeElement).toBe(root.querySelector('input'));
});
```

### Row selection with Ctrl and Shift: logic in a helper, applied by the handler

```html
<sn-resource name="files" src="/api/files" items="files" key="id"></sn-resource>

<!-- the logic is in rowClick() (row-select.helpers.js); the handler only applies its result -->
<section data-sn-state="{ sel: noSelection() }" data-sn-let="{ ids: files.map(f => f.id) }">
  <p data-sn-text="sel.keys.length + ' selected'"></p>
  <ul role="listbox" aria-multiselectable="true">
    <template data-sn-for="f in files">
      <li role="option" data-sn-attr="{'aria-selected': sel.keys.includes(f.id) ? 'true' : 'false'}"
          data-sn-on-click="sel = rowClick($event, sel, f.id, ids)" data-sn-text="f.name"></li>
    </template>
  </ul>
  <button data-sn-show="sel.keys.length" data-sn-on-click="sel = noSelection()">Clear</button>
</section>
```

```js
// Helpers hold the logic; the page applies their result (`sel = rowClick(…)`).
// They are pure: the same arguments give the same result, nothing else is read or changed,
// so they are unit-tested without a page.

/** No row selected. */
export const noSelection = () => ({ keys: [], anchor: null });

/**
 * The selection after a click on the row `key`, as a file manager does it. `sel` is
 * `{ keys, anchor }`, `keys` the rows' keys in the order they are shown.
 * - a click selects only that row;
 * - Ctrl (Cmd on a Mac) adds or removes that row;
 * - Shift selects the rows from the anchor (the last row clicked without Shift) to this one;
 *   with Ctrl too, it adds them to the selection.
 */
export function rowClick(event, sel, key, keys) {
  const add = event.ctrlKey || event.metaKey;
  if (event.shiftKey && sel.anchor != null && keys.includes(sel.anchor)) {
    const a = keys.indexOf(sel.anchor), b = keys.indexOf(key);
    const range = keys.slice(Math.min(a, b), Math.max(a, b) + 1);
    const chosen = new Set([...(add ? sel.keys : []), ...range]);
    return { keys: keys.filter((k) => chosen.has(k)), anchor: sel.anchor };
  }
  if (add) {
    const chosen = sel.keys.includes(key) ? sel.keys.filter((k) => k !== key) : [...sel.keys, key];
    return { keys: keys.filter((k) => chosen.includes(k)), anchor: key };
  }
  return { keys: [key], anchor: key };
}
```

```ts
import { describe, expect, test } from 'vitest';
import { render, mockRequests } from '@tiaforge-ui/sinter/testing';
import * as helpers from './row-select.helpers.js';
import page from './row-select.html?raw';

const { rowClick, noSelection } = helpers;

// the helper: pure, so tested with plain values
describe('rowClick', () => {
  const keys = ['a', 'b', 'c', 'd'];
  const click = (init: Partial<MouseEvent> = {}) => ({ ctrlKey: false, metaKey: false, shiftKey: false, ...init }) as MouseEvent;
  test('a click selects only that row and makes it the anchor', () => {
    expect(rowClick(click(), { keys: ['a', 'c'], anchor: 'a' }, 'b', keys)).toEqual({ keys: ['b'], anchor: 'b' });
  });
  test('Ctrl or Cmd adds or removes the row, in display order', () => {
    expect(rowClick(click({ ctrlKey: true }), { keys: ['c'], anchor: 'c' }, 'a', keys)).toEqual({ keys: ['a', 'c'], anchor: 'a' });
    expect(rowClick(click({ metaKey: true }), { keys: ['a', 'c'], anchor: 'a' }, 'c', keys)).toEqual({ keys: ['a'], anchor: 'c' });
  });
  test('Shift selects from the anchor, in either direction; with Ctrl it adds', () => {
    expect(rowClick(click({ shiftKey: true }), { keys: ['b'], anchor: 'b' }, 'd', keys)).toEqual({ keys: ['b', 'c', 'd'], anchor: 'b' });
    expect(rowClick(click({ shiftKey: true }), { keys: ['c'], anchor: 'c' }, 'a', keys)).toEqual({ keys: ['a', 'b', 'c'], anchor: 'c' });
    expect(rowClick(click({ shiftKey: true, ctrlKey: true }), { keys: ['a', 'd'], anchor: 'd' }, 'c', keys)).toEqual({ keys: ['a', 'c', 'd'], anchor: 'd' });
  });
  test('Shift without an anchor (or a removed one) is a plain click', () => {
    expect(rowClick(click({ shiftKey: true }), noSelection(), 'c', keys)).toEqual({ keys: ['c'], anchor: 'c' });
    expect(rowClick(click({ shiftKey: true }), { keys: ['x'], anchor: 'x' }, 'c', keys)).toEqual({ keys: ['c'], anchor: 'c' });
  });
});

// the page: the handler applies the helper's result
test('click, Ctrl+click and Shift+click select rows', async () => {
  const requests = mockRequests({ 'GET /api/files': { files: ['a', 'b', 'c', 'd'].map((id) => ({ id, name: id.toUpperCase() })) } });
  const { root, flush, settle } = await render(page, { requests, helpers });
  await settle();
  const rows = () => [...root.querySelectorAll('li')];
  const click = (i: number, init: MouseEventInit = {}) => rows()[i]!.dispatchEvent(new MouseEvent('click', { bubbles: true, ...init }));
  const selected = () => rows().filter((li) => li.getAttribute('aria-selected') === 'true').map((li) => li.textContent);

  click(1);
  click(3, { shiftKey: true });
  await flush();
  expect(selected()).toEqual(['B', 'C', 'D']);
  click(0, { ctrlKey: true });
  await flush();
  expect(selected()).toEqual(['A', 'B', 'C', 'D']);
  expect(root.querySelector('p')!.textContent).toBe('4 selected');
  root.querySelector('button')!.click();
  await flush();
  expect(selected()).toEqual([]);
});
```

### Run an action from a handler: mark a mail read once its body has loaded, and a shortcut

```html
<!doctype html>
<html>
<body data-sn-state="{ open: null, error: '' }" data-sn-on-keydown-e="run('archive')">
  <sn-resource name="messages" src="/api/messages" items="messages" key="id"></sn-resource>
  <!-- loads when a mail opens; once its body is there, an unread mail is marked read -->
  <sn-resource name="body" src="/api/messages/{open.id}/body" when="open"
               then="$result && !open.is_read && run('mark-read')"></sn-resource>

  <ul>
    <template data-sn-for="m in messages">
      <li data-sn-class="{unread: !m.is_read}" data-sn-on-click="open = m" data-sn-text="m.subject"></li>
    </template>
  </ul>
  <article data-sn-show="open" data-sn-text="body && body.text"></article>

  <!-- no visible control: the element only carries the action (data-sn-call works the same) -->
  <span hidden id="mark-read" data-sn-patch="/api/messages/{open.id}" data-sn-body="{is_read: true}"
        data-sn-optimistic="patch('messages', open, {is_read: true})"
        data-sn-catch="error = $error.message"></span>
  <!-- the button and E run one action; while it is disabled, E does nothing either -->
  <button id="archive" data-sn-post="/api/messages/{open.id}/archive" data-sn-attr="{disabled: !open}"
          data-sn-optimistic="remove('messages', open)" data-sn-then="open = null">Archive (E)</button>
  <p role="alert" data-sn-text="error"></p>
</body>
</html>
```

```ts
import { expect, test } from 'vitest';
import { checkPage } from '@tiaforge-ui/sinter/check';
import { render, mockRequests } from '@tiaforge-ui/sinter/testing';
import page from './run-action.html?raw';

const MESSAGES = { messages: [{ id: 1, subject: 'Hello', is_read: false }, { id: 2, subject: 'Lunch?', is_read: true }] };
const key = (el: Element, k: string) => el.dispatchEvent(new KeyboardEvent('keydown', { key: k, bubbles: true, cancelable: true }));

test('opening an unread mail marks it read once its body has loaded; a read one sends nothing', async () => {
  const requests = mockRequests({
    'GET /api/messages': MESSAGES,
    'GET /api/messages/1/body': { text: 'Hi there' },
    'GET /api/messages/2/body': { text: 'At noon?' },
    'PATCH /api/messages/1': null,
  });
  const { root, settle } = await render(page, { requests });
  await settle();
  const rows = () => [...root.querySelectorAll('li')];
  expect(rows().map((li) => li.className)).toEqual(['unread', '']);

  rows()[0]!.click();
  await settle();
  expect(root.querySelector('article')!.textContent).toBe('Hi there');
  expect(requests.calls.at(-1)).toMatchObject({ method: 'PATCH', path: '/api/messages/1', body: { is_read: true } });
  expect(rows()[0]!.className).toBe('');

  rows()[1]!.click();
  await settle();
  expect(requests.calls.filter((c) => c.method === 'PATCH')).toHaveLength(1);
});

test('a failed mark-read rolls back and shows the error', async () => {
  const requests = mockRequests({
    'GET /api/messages': MESSAGES,
    'GET /api/messages/1/body': { text: 'Hi there' },
    'PATCH /api/messages/1': { status: 503, body: { message: 'Mail server unavailable' } },
  });
  const { root, settle } = await render(page, { requests });
  await settle();
  root.querySelector('li')!.click();
  await settle();
  expect(root.querySelector('li')!.className).toBe('unread');
  expect(root.querySelector('[role=alert]')!.textContent).toBe('Mail server unavailable');
});

test('E archives the open mail through the button; with no mail open the button is disabled and E does nothing', async () => {
  const requests = mockRequests({
    'GET /api/messages': MESSAGES,
    'GET /api/messages/2/body': { text: 'At noon?' },
    'POST /api/messages/2/archive': null,
  });
  const { root, settle } = await render(page, { requests });
  await settle();
  key(root, 'e');
  await settle();
  expect(requests.calls.map((c) => c.method)).toEqual(['GET']);

  root.querySelectorAll('li')[1]!.click();
  await settle();
  key(root, 'e');
  await settle();
  expect(requests.calls.at(-1)).toMatchObject({ method: 'POST', path: '/api/messages/2/archive' });
  expect([...root.querySelectorAll('li')].map((li) => li.textContent)).toEqual(['Hello']);
  expect(root.querySelector('button')!.disabled).toBe(true);
});

test('sinter check: run() names an element with an action', () => {
  expect(checkPage(page).filter((d) => d.severity === 'error')).toEqual([]);
  const [d] = checkPage(page.replace("run('mark-read')", "run('mark-raed')")).filter((x) => x.severity === 'error');
  expect([d!.code, d!.message]).toEqual(['SN311', 'no element `id="mark-raed"` on this page. Did you mean `mark-read`?']);
});
```

### First paint: page chrome that renders before the script

```html
<!-- First paint: what renders before the page module has run. Chrome stays outside data templates (or in a
     data-sn-if over state), so the early chunk renders it before the first paint: messages in the language
     picked before the paint, the current page from literal state, the persisted collapse. Only what needs
     data waits in a template for the page module. -->
<body data-sn-state="{ here: '/mail/' }">
  <sn-resource name="user" src="/api/user"></sn-resource>
  <nav data-sn-attr="{'aria-label': m.nav()}" data-sn-state="{ collapsed: false }">
    <input type="checkbox" data-sn-model="collapsed" data-sn-persist="nav-collapsed" data-sn-attr="{'aria-label': m.collapse()}">
    <a href="/mail/" data-sn-attr="{'aria-current': here === '/mail/' ? 'page' : null}"><span data-sn-text="m.mail()"></span></a>
    <a href="/calendar/" data-sn-attr="{'aria-current': here === '/calendar/' ? 'page' : null}"><span data-sn-text="m.calendar()"></span></a>
    <!-- needs the user: renders when the page module has loaded it -->
    <template data-sn-if="user"><span data-sn-text="user.name"></span></template>
  </nav>
</body>
```

```ts
import { expect, test } from 'vitest';
import { firstPaint, memoryStorage, mockRequests, render } from '@tiaforge-ui/sinter/testing';
import page from './first-paint.html?raw';

// the message files (see the Messages recipe)
const messages = {
  en: { nav: 'Main navigation', collapse: 'Collapse menu', mail: 'Mail', calendar: 'Calendar' },
  de: { nav: 'Hauptnavigation', collapse: 'Menü einklappen', mail: 'E-Mail', calendar: 'Kalender' },
};

test('before the page module: messages in the visitor\'s language, the current page, the persisted collapse', async () => {
  const storage = memoryStorage();
  storage.setItem('locale', 'de');
  storage.setItem('sn:nav-collapsed', 'true');
  const { root } = await firstPaint(page, { messages, storage });
  expect([...root.querySelectorAll('a')].map((a) => [a.textContent, a.getAttribute('aria-current')])).toEqual([['E-Mail', 'page'], ['Kalender', null]]);
  expect(root.querySelector('input')!.checked).toBe(true);
  expect(root.querySelector('nav > span')).toBeNull();  // the user's name waits for its data
});

test('the page module takes over without changing what was shown, then fills in data', async () => {
  const storage = memoryStorage();
  storage.setItem('sn:nav-collapsed', 'true');
  let shown = '';
  const requests = mockRequests({ 'GET /api/user': { name: 'Ada' } });
  const { root, settle } = await render(page, {
    messages, storage, requests,
    firstPaint: { afterEarly: () => { shown = document.querySelector('nav')!.outerHTML; } },
  });
  expect(root.querySelector('nav')!.outerHTML).toBe(shown);
  await settle();
  expect(root.querySelector('nav')!.textContent).toContain('Ada');
  expect(root.querySelector('input')!.checked).toBe(true);
});
```

### Messages: m.key() from the inlang files, switching without a reload

```html
<!-- Messages: m.key() from the inlang files (project.inlang, messages/{locale}.json), with {param}s.
     The build gives this page one small file per language with only the keys it calls; the language is
     picked before the first paint. $locale = … switches without a reload. -->
<body data-sn-state="{ lang: $locale }">
  <sn-resource name="inbox" src="/api/inbox" type="any"></sn-resource>
  <h1 data-sn-text="m.inbox_title()"></h1>
  <p data-sn-text="m.inbox_count({ count: inbox ? inbox.unread : 0 })"></p>
  <select data-sn-model="lang" data-sn-on-change="$locale = lang" data-sn-attr="{'aria-label': m.language()}">
    <option value="en">English</option>
    <option value="de">Deutsch</option>
  </select>
</body>
```

```ts
import { expect, test } from 'vitest';
import { memoryStorage, mockRequests, render } from '@tiaforge-ui/sinter/testing';
import page from './messages.html?raw';

// messages/en.json and messages/de.json (the base language first)
const messages = {
  en: { inbox_title: 'Inbox', inbox_count: '{count} unread', language: 'Language' },
  de: { inbox_title: 'Posteingang', inbox_count: '{count} ungelesen', language: 'Sprache' },
};

test('the stored language, with parameters; switching re-renders without a reload', async () => {
  const storage = memoryStorage();
  storage.setItem('locale', 'de');
  const requests = mockRequests({ 'GET /api/inbox': { unread: 3 } });
  const { root, settle, flush, navigations } = await render(page, { messages, storage, requests });
  await settle();
  expect(root.querySelector('h1')!.textContent).toBe('Posteingang');
  expect(root.querySelector('p')!.textContent).toBe('3 ungelesen');

  const select = root.querySelector('select')!;
  select.value = 'en';
  select.dispatchEvent(new Event('change', { bubbles: true }));
  await flush();
  await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 0));
  await flush();
  expect(root.querySelector('h1')!.textContent).toBe('Inbox');
  expect(root.querySelector('p')!.textContent).toBe('3 unread');
  expect(document.documentElement.lang).toBe('en');
  expect(navigations).toEqual([]);
});
```

## Type checking

`npx sinter check` type-checks every expression with the project's TypeScript (pages and options come from the Vite config). `sinter({ typecheck: true })` runs it in `vite build`.

- `<sn-resource … type="Contact[]">`: the type of what `items` selects, using names exported by `src/sinter.types.ts`. `type="any"` opts out; no `type` is warning SN504.
- `sinter({ openapi: 'openapi.yml' })`: resources without `type` are matched to a GET operation by `src` (server prefix stripped, `{…}` matches a path parameter) and typed from its JSON response at `items`. Every build then checks `items`/`total` against the schema (SN308) and query parameter names (SN505).
- State takes a JSDoc cast where the literal is not enough: `data-sn-state="{ editing: /** @type {Contact|null} */ (null) }"`.
- Actions matched in the spec: `data-sn-body` is checked against the request schema, `$result` in `then` has the response type.
- `$result` in `<sn-resource then>` has the resource's type (`type`, OpenAPI, or a `call`'s result).
- `<sn-event … type="ContactEvent">` types the payload; `item` must fit the resource's item, `set` part of it, and `then` is checked against it; `cursor` reads the item. No `type` on an event with payload expressions is warning SN506.
- In the URL, body, call arguments and confirm of an element `run('id')` starts (not a form), `$event` is `RunEvent<…>` (no event when run): guard reads with `$event && $event.shiftKey`.
- SN509 (`run-cycle`) is opt-in: `sinter check --check-cycles`, or `sinter({ checkCycles: true })` for the build, `sinter check` and `sinter lsp`. It reports `then`/`catch` handlers that start each other again through `run()` (and `refresh()`), with every step.
- Errors are SN208 at the HTML position, with TypeScript's message. Null checks are off. In tests: `checkPage(html, { files, openapi })` from `@tiaforge-ui/sinter/check`.

## First paint

The built page shows its chrome before the page module has run; the page bundle is not render-blocking and is `async` (it does not wait for stylesheets), so it may run while the body is still being parsed: keep app code at module top level from reading the body, and don't read an island's children or later siblings in `connectedCallback`. The page module waits for the parse and for the early file before it mounts.

- Build-time constants are written into the HTML: bindings outside templates that read only literal `data-sn-state` fields and constants (`aria-current` from `here === '/mail/'`). No helpers.
- Each page gets an early chunk, bundled into one file with nothing to import and loaded `type="module" blocking="render"` before the page module (one request before the first paint): first `src/sinter.early.ts` (optional app code), then, once, the bindings outside `data-sn-for` templates that need no data: they read state fields whose initial value needs no data, persisted values (read from `sn:<key>` in localStorage), `$locale` and helpers. A `data-sn-if` of that kind renders its branch; the page module adopts it. Only the helpers and message members those bindings call are included. Modules it shares with the page bundle are copies: state the early module sets must be set again by the page bundle (sinter's messages share theirs through a global).
- Resources, `$url`, `$now`, `$meta`, `$el`, loops and the built-in formatters (`date()`, …) wait for the page module. The runtime then owns every binding; its first write changes nothing.
- Every origin a literal `src` names (resources and streams) gets `<link rel="preconnect" crossorigin>`. Data requests start before the page module: a resource with a literal same-origin `src` and no `when` gets `<link rel="preload" as="fetch" crossorigin>`; one whose URL reads only state that needs no data, persisted values, `$now`, `$url` and helpers is requested by the early file. The runtime takes those responses at the end of its middleware chain when the request is unchanged (no header or credentials added), so response middleware still runs; changed requests are sent again. Not for paginated, `each`, `call` or embedded resources. A resource only elements inside `<dialog>`s read is requested with low priority (`fetchpriority="low"` on its preload, `priority: 'low'` on its fetch).
- Next-page data: when the pointer rests on a same-origin link to another page of the app (65 ms), it has focus, or a press or touch starts on it, that page's resources whose `src`/`when` read only `$url`, constants and helpers are requested (low priority, through the middleware; data this page loaded from the same request is handed over without one). The next page shows them at once and revalidates; `$meta.<name>.loadedAt` stays null until the server answers. Entries are taken once, kept 30 s, dropped after any mutation; a failed prefetch never triggers `onUnauthorized`. Nothing to write: give pages `data-sn-path` patterns so links like `/article/slug` match. `sinter({ prefetch: false })` turns it off; test with `render(html, { pages: { 'article.html': articleHtml } })`. In Chromium, pages also get Speculation Rules for those links (`sinter({ speculation: 'prefetch' | 'prerender' | false })`, default `'prefetch'`); under a CSP add `'inline-speculation-rules'` to `script-src`. A prerendered page connects streams once shown and refetches then.
- Browsers without `blocking="render"` (Firefox, as of 159) would paint the body before the early file has rendered (a persisted collapsed rail shown open for a frame) and run CSS transitions from that state. There the page's first classic script (the language picker, else `assets/sinter-paint-<hash>.js`, on pages with an early file) sets `visibility: hidden` on `<html>` and turns transitions off (a constructed stylesheet: no inline style for the CSP) until the early file has rendered and the stylesheets have applied; after a layout flush both are back. The hiding lasts 2 s at most; without the early file, the window's `load` ends it. Chromium: nothing changes. Apps need no workaround for transitions on load.
- The build prints each page's early file size (gzip) and warns over `sinter({ earlyBudget })` (default 10000 bytes), naming the largest modules: keep heavy imports out of early code.
- Keep page chrome outside data templates: `<template data-sn-if="user">` around the navigation hides it until the user has loaded.
- `sinter({ firstPaint: false })` turns it off. Test with `firstPaint(html, { helpers, storage, early })` from the testing module (`early` stands for `src/sinter.early.ts`), and `render(html, { firstPaint: { early, afterEarly } })` for the takeover.

## Messages

- With an inlang project (`project.inlang/settings.json`, message files `messages/{locale}.json` of plain `"key": "text with {param}"`), `m.key()` / `m.key({ param })` in markup are sinter's built-in messages. App code: `import { m } from '@tiaforge-ui/sinter/messages'`, typed by the generated `src/sinter.messages.d.ts`. Unknown keys are SN206, wrong or missing params SN208 (`sinter check`). Only `m.key`: `m[key]` or passing `m` on fails the build; a dynamic choice is a switch.
- The build emits one file per page and language with only the keys the page calls (markup and its modules); a missing translation is the base language, reported at build. No plurals or variants.
- Before the first paint a tiny classic script picks the language (localStorage `locale`, else `navigator.languages`, else the base), sets `<html lang>` and loads the page's language file render-blocking: on every page that calls `m`, in its markup or in a helper, action or island it bundles. `$locale = 'de'` switches without a reload (stores the choice, loads that file, re-renders). Don't `configure({ locale })`: sinter is the locale source.
- Tests: `render(html, { messages: { en: {…}, de: {…} }, locale })`. An app without an inlang project ships none of this.

## Deploying streams

Each open EventSource holds one HTTP connection, and HTTP/1.1 allows 6 per origin: with more than 5 tabs open, pages stop loading. Serve streams over HTTP/2 (any TLS reverse proxy such as nginx or Caddy) or use the WebSocket transport; dev builds warn about HTTP/1.1.

## Editors

`npx sinter lsp --stdio` is a language server for the project's HTML files: sinter's diagnostics as you type (partials checked through the pages that include them), and with TypeScript 7 type errors, hover, completion in expressions, go to definition and a did-you-mean quick fix; "Extract to helper" moves an expression into a typed function of the helpers module. VS Code: the extension in `editors/vscode`. Setup for Neovim, Helix and Emacs: `docs/editors.md`. Every diagnostic links to its explanation in `docs/diagnostics.md`.

## Testing

Write a test next to the markup. `@tiaforge-ui/sinter/testing` compiles the page with the real compiler and mounts it:

- `render(html, { requests, streams, url, locale, now, helpers, actions, files, storage, session, firstPaint })` → `{ root, app, flush, settle, advance, navigations, window }`. Pass one `memoryStorage()` as `session` to two renders to test what carries over between page loads (the `cache` attribute). A full document keeps its `<html>` attributes, so state and `data-sn-persist` on `<html>` work as in the browser.
- `mockRequests({ 'GET /api/x': json | {status, body} | (call) => … })`: records `calls`; responses are held until `settle()`; an unmatched request fails the test and lists the routes.
- `mockStream()`: `emit(name, payload)`, `drop()`, `connected`. A stream URL with no mock uses the transport from `configure({ transport })`, so a custom transport can be tested over a fake connection (see the SignalR recipe).
- `flush()` runs the scheduler (optimistic changes are visible), `settle()` finishes requests, queues and debounces, `advance(ms)` moves sinter's clock.
- `firstPaint(html, { helpers, files, storage, early })` → `{ root, html }`: the page as the browser shows it before the page module runs (build-time constants, then the early chunk). `render(…, { firstPaint: { early, afterEarly } })` mounts over that first paint; `afterEarly` runs in between, so a test can watch what mounting changes.
